usage: papers init [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                   [--porcelain] [--name-template NAME_TEMPLATE]
                   [--name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM]
                   [--name-author-sep NAME_AUTHOR_SEP]
                   [--name-title-word-num NAME_TITLE_WORD_NUM]
                   [--name-title-word-size NAME_TITLE_WORD_SIZE]
                   [--name-title-length NAME_TITLE_LENGTH]
                   [--name-title-sep NAME_TITLE_SEP]
                   [--name-unknown-template NAME_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE]
                   [--name-unknown-strict | --no-name-unknown-strict]
                   [--key-template KEY_TEMPLATE]
                   [--key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM]
                   [--key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP]
                   [--key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM]
                   [--key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE]
                   [--key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH]
                   [--key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP]
                   [--key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE]
                   [--key-unknown-strict | --no-key-unknown-strict]
                   [--bibtex BIBTEX] [--filesdir FILESDIR] [--pool PATH]
                   [--shallow] [--global] [--paths {relative,absolute}]
                   [--editor EDITOR]
                   [DIR]

create a library in the current directory, or in DIR (created if missing): a
self-contained library (its own entries and files, no pool), or with --pool
PATH a shallow library, which takes its entries from the library PATH and
links to its files. It asks no questions: every setting has a default (from
the global configuration, or built in), the options below override them, and
later changes go through `papers config`.

positional arguments:
  DIR                   directory of the library (default: the current
                        directory); --bibtex and --filesdir are relative to it

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error
  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex file (default: papers.bib, or the first .bib
                        file of the directory)
  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: files, or an existing pdfs/,
                        papers/... folder)
  --pool PATH           a shallow library that uses the library PATH as pool
                        (a path relative to the library; PATH must be a
                        library without pool): `papers add` looks in PATH
                        first and adds the new entries and their files to it,
                        and the library links to the files of PATH. Default:
                        no pool, a self-contained library
  --shallow             same as --pool with the default library (`papers
                        config --global default`)
  --global              also register the library as the default library (used
                        outside of any library, and by --shallow); DIR is
                        required (`papers init . --global` for the current
                        directory)
  --paths {relative,absolute}
                        file links in the bibtex relative to the bibtex
                        directory, or absolute (default: relative)
  --editor EDITOR       command to open a text editor; it must wait until the
                        editor is closed, e.g. vim or "subl -w"

filename format:
  --name-template NAME_TEMPLATE
                        python template for renaming files (default:
                        {authorX}_{year}_{title})
  --name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the filename (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 2)
  --name-author-sep NAME_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the filename (default: _)
  --name-title-word-num NAME_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the filename
                        (default: 100)
  --name-title-word-size NAME_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the filename (default: 1)
  --name-title-length NAME_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the filename (the last
                        words are dropped until it fits; a longer first word
                        is cut) (default: 100)
  --name-title-sep NAME_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the filename (default:
                        -)
  --name-unknown-template NAME_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the filename of an entry without author,
                        year or title (default: unknown_{doi_or_id})
  --name-unknown-strict, --no-name-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: False)

bibtex key format:
  --key-template KEY_TEMPLATE
                        python template for generating keys (default:
                        {author}{year}). The template applies to entries
                        generated from a PDF or a DOI; entries added from a
                        bibtex file keep their original key unless
                        -u/--update-key is passed.
  --key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the key (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 2)
  --key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the key (default: _)
  --key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the key (default:
                        100)
  --key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the key (default: 1)
  --key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the key (the last words
                        are dropped until it fits; a longer first word is cut)
                        (default: 100)
  --key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the key (default: -)
  --key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the key of an entry without author, year
                        or title (default: {doi_})
  --key-unknown-strict, --no-key-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: False)
